correctness.rationale: For each i the centred coordinate satisfies 2Xi=(Xi+Xj)+(Xi+Xk)−(Xj+Xk). Thus success projects into a central interval of length at most 3ε; the one-dimensional marginal gives the upper bound for every Borel coupling, including at ε=0. Independently normalize to ε=1/3: for T uniform on [0,1], randomly permute ((5+T)/6,(3−T)/6,(1+T)/6), with independent equally likely simultaneous reflection. The three raw pair sums are 4/3, 1+T/3 and 2/3; reflection preserves the tolerance. The six affine marginals range over the six successive sixths, each selected with probability 1/6, so each mixed coordinate is uniform. For 0<ε<1/3 scale this successful coupling toward 1/2 by 3ε and assign it precisely the marginal mass 3ε of the resulting interval. On the complementary branch take uniform marginals on the two outer parts; this branch cannot succeed by the projection bound. The threshold coupling works unchanged above 1/3. The inspected rational diagnostic is finite and not needed for this continuum proof.
residual_risks: This verifies arbitrary Borel dependence, not attainability under absolute continuity or prescribed bivariate margins.

The projection bound alone does not show that three marginal requirements can be saturated by the same law. The piecewise-affine attaining coupling gives the exact attainable guarantee and feasibility threshold, useful for bounded-error dependence design and as a benchmark for multistochastic event optimization.
